ADDED i2: Two instants built from the same arguments compare as equal. The negative nanosecond adjustment (-3113) is normalised: one second is borrowed, so the stored sec
ADDED i3: Instants with the seconds and nano arguments swapped represent different points on the time-line and are therefore not equal.
ADDED i4: Comparing a {@code TaiInstant} to a plain {@code Object} returns false.
ADDED i5: An instant is always equal to itself.
ADDED i6: Changing the nano-of-second produces an instant that is not equal to the original, while leaving the original untouched (the class is immutable).
ADDED i7: Replacing the seconds with a smaller value (while keeping the original nanos) yields an instant that is later on the time-line, so the original is before it.
ADDED i8: An instant is never before itself.
ADDED i9: The instant with the larger nano-of-second is after the one whose nanos were reset to zero (the seconds are identical).
ADDED i10: An earlier instant is not after a later one.
ADDED i11: Subtracting a zero duration returns the same instance unchanged.
ADDED i12: Subtracting 20 milliseconds reduces the nano-of-second by 20,000,000 while leaving the seconds unchanged and the original instant intact.
ADDED i13: Adding a zero duration returns the same instance unchanged.
ADDED i14: Sanity check on {@link UtcInstant#plus(Duration)} used as a fixture here: adding a negative millisecond duration adjusts the nano-of-day.
ADDED i15: {@code withNano} rejects a value equal to 1,000,000,000 (the upper bound is 999,999,999).
ADDED i17: {@code withNano} rejects a negative value.

ADDED i19: Parsing a string whose nanosecond part is too short fails internally while the regex matcher is queried before a successful match.

ADDED i22: Parsing a buffer of blank characters does not match the expected format and raises a {@link DateTimeParseException}.
ADDED i24: The duration of an instant until itself can be computed without altering the instant.
ADDED i25: Converting a TAI instant to a {@code UtcInstant} yields the expected nano-of-day.
ADDED i26: Converting to an {@code Instant} leaves the source TAI instant unchanged.
ADDED i27: {@code toString} formats the instant as {@code {seconds}.{nanos}s(TAI)} with exactly nine nanosecond digits.
ADDED i28: Building a TAI instant from a (mocked) "now" {@code Instant} produces the expected TAI seconds and nanos.
ADDED i29: {@code hashCode} can be computed without altering the instant's fields.
ADDED i30: Converting a null {@code UtcInstant} fails with a {@link NullPointerException} raised within the leap-second rules.
